components.css: :host{--wall:#121318;--wall-2:#1b1c23;--paper:#f2eadb;--muted:#b3ab9d;--red:#e2231a;--yellow:#f2c200;--line:rgba(242,234,219,.16);--news:#efe3c8;--ink:#111;--c-yellow:#f7c600;--c-red:#e2231a;--c-blue:#1d5fb4;--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)} .ds-wall{background:var(--wall);padding:24px} .ds-toast{font-family:Archivo,system-ui,sans-serif;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;padding:10px 12px 10px 16px;border-radius:6px;background:var(--paper);color:var(--wall);font-weight:700;font-size:14px;box-shadow:0 12px 34px rgba(0,0,0,.5);animation:ds-toast-in .35s var(--ease-out)} .ds-toast button{font-family:Archivo,system-ui,sans-serif;flex:none;border:0;border-radius:4px;background:var(--wall);color:var(--paper);font-weight:800;font-size:13px;padding:6px 10px;cursor:pointer} .ds-toast button:hover{background:#000} .ds-toast button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--wall);outline-offset:3px} @keyframes ds-toast-in{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(8px)}}

narrative.overview:
The site is a dark room with a wall of red lacquered ledges, and every MCU film is an original comic standing on it. Issues you haven't watched yet wait in their clear plastic bags, drained to grey. Watching one takes it out of the bag, brings back its color and stamps it **VISTO!**. The next issue sits pulled forward with a yellow label, and the last spot on the wall holds the premiere edition in a graded slab. The wall is the frame for everything: the countdown, the numbers and the progress bar are printed over its top and bottom edges like gallery signage, and they never compete with the covers.

Pulling an issue off the wall opens it into a full comic-book page: newsprint, ink-outlined panels, Bangers lettering, starburst sound effects, and a halftone red action panel where you hit **MARCAR!**. The shelf is quiet and nocturnal; the page is loud and printed. The comic language may come out onto the wall for real moments (finishing the marathon, the premiere arriving), but the wall's everyday chrome stays restrained so the covers carry the color.

Real covers are the imagery. Color on the wall is earned: a cover only gets its color back when the film is watched, and the brand red and yellow are kept for the deadline, the next film, and progress.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, warm-black wall with off-white "paper" text; the comic covers are the only full-color element at rest.
One variable sans (Archivo) runs the wall, carrying hierarchy through scale and width axis alone; the countdown is a single monumental condensed numeral.
The comic page switches to a full print vocabulary: newsprint dots, 4px ink outlines, flat yellow/red/blue, hard offset shadows, rotated lettering.
Watched vs not watched is shown with material (bag, desaturation, stamp), not with badges or checkmarks.
On phones a lighter mode is required: fewer, smaller textures, and the same hierarchy at reduced sizes.

rules.name: The Earned Color Rule
rules.body: At rest the wall is greyscale plus paper; covers come back to color only when watched. Red and yellow on the wall's chrome are reserved for the deadline, the next film and progress. Never tint an unwatched cover or add decorative color to the HUD.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Next Rule
rules.body: On the wall, `yellow` marks the single next action (the Próximo card, the next ledge label, the pace that tells you whether you'll make it). If something is yellow and it isn't about what comes next, it's wrong.

rules.name: The Two Yellows Rule
rules.body: `yellow` belongs to the wall, `comic-yellow` to the printed page. They are near-identical by design but don't swap them; the comic one is the warmer process yellow that sits on newsprint.

rules.name: The Width-Axis Rule
rules.body: On the wall, hierarchy comes from scale and the `wdth` axis, never from a second family. Numerals squeeze (62–70), labels stretch (110–112). All counting numbers use tabular figures.

rules.name: The Letterer's Rule
rules.body: Bangers is for what a comic would shout (titles, sound effects, data values) and always carries an ink stroke drawn under the fill (`paint-order: stroke fill`). Running text is never set in Bangers.

rules.name: The Material State Rule
rules.body: Watched vs not watched is shown with material and light: in the bag, desaturated (12% saturation) and dimmed (42% brightness) versus out of the bag, full color, stamped. Never reduce it to a badge or a checkmark on the wall itself; the text list is where checkmarks live.

rules.name: The Hard Shadow Rule
rules.body: On the comic page, shadows have zero blur and use ink. Soft shadows belong only to the wall.

dos: **Do** let the covers be the only full color on the wall at rest; HUD chrome stays wall, paper, `muted` and hairlines.
**Do** keep `yellow` on the wall for the single next action and pace, and `red` for the brand, progress and the VISTO! stamp.
**Do** set every counting number in Archivo with tabular figures, squeezed on the `wdth` axis (62–70).
**Do** use 4px ink outlines, square corners and zero-blur ink shadows on anything that lives on the comic page.
**Do** stroke Bangers lettering in ink under the fill (2–3px, `paint-order: stroke fill`).
**Do** bring comic lettering and bursts onto the wall for real milestones (marathon finished, premiere day), and only then.
**Do** keep the focus ring visible: 3px yellow on the wall, 3px comic blue on the page.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion` and the lightweight phone mode in every new 3D or animated piece.
donts: **Don't** add decorative color, gradients or glows to the HUD; it fades into the wall with its own gradients only.
**Don't** show watched state on the wall with badges, ribbons or checkmarks; use the bag, the desaturation and the stamp.
**Don't** use soft blurred shadows or rounded panels on the comic page, or hard ink offsets on the wall.
**Don't** set running text in Bangers, or bring in a second sans for the wall.
**Don't** swap `yellow` and `comic-yellow` between the two surfaces.
**Don't** replace the real comic covers with illustrations, posters or generated art.
